knowledgePolicy.nativeAuthorityRule: A normative standard or platform rule can be authoritative only inside its own exact native scope. It does not gain Game semantic or creative authority.
knowledgePolicy.designTheoryRule: Theory, measurement models and practitioner frameworks are lenses/hypotheses unless an exact claim is supported by matching evidence.
knowledgePolicy.teardownRule: Developer postmortems are primary accounts of one project. Extract mechanisms, confounds, falsifiers and transfer risks; never recipes.
knowledgePolicy.skillRule: Skills package reusable instructions; tools execute; MCP transports/discovers. Installing or finding a Skill never transfers domain authority.

authorityClasses.NORMATIVE_STANDARD: Formal normative source in native scope
authorityClasses.PLATFORM_GUIDANCE: Official platform guidance/rules in native scope

sources.title: ISO 9241-210:2019 Human-centred design for interactive systems
sources.evidenceLimit: Applies to human-centred design practice; does not define game quality, fun, or a universal game-development lifecycle.

sources.title: ISO 9241-11:2018 Usability: Definitions and concepts
sources.evidenceLimit: Defines usability concepts but explicitly does not prescribe a particular design/evaluation method.

sources.title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2
sources.evidenceLimit: Normative for web accessibility scope; not a complete game accessibility specification or gameplay design framework.

sources.title: Xbox Accessibility Guidelines V3.2
sources.evidenceLimit: Microsoft explicitly frames XAGs as best-practice guardrails/idea catalysts, not legal compliance certification.

sources.title: XAG 107: Input
extractedIdeas: input mechanisms should not assume one physical ability profile
sources.evidenceLimit: Platform guidance; exact implementation depends on game/platform mechanics.

sources.title: XAG 101: Text display
sources.evidenceLimit: Platform guidance, not proof that a particular game UI is accessible to a specific population.

sources.title: XAG 104: Subtitles and captions
extractedIdeas: speech and non-speech cues need alternatives
sources.evidenceLimit: Does not establish that captions alone resolve all hearing-related barriers.

sources.title: XAG 105: Audio accessibility
extractedIdeas: separate volume channels can support diverse needs
sources.evidenceLimit: Guidance for accessibility; artistic mix choices still require game-specific evaluation.

sources.title: XAG 117: Visual distractions and motion settings
sources.evidenceLimit: Platform guidance; does not imply one universal FOV/camera value.

sources.title: XAG 108: Game difficulty options
extractedIdeas: experienced difficulty emerges from player abilities relative to barriers

sources.title: XAG 109: Objective clarity

sources.title: XAG 103: Additional channels for visual and audio cues
extractedIdeas: critical cues can be represented through multiple sensory channels

sources.title: Game Accessibility Guidelines — Full List

sources.title: IGDA Game Accessibility SIG — Resources for game developers

sources.title: Designing for games
sources.evidenceLimit: Apple-platform guidance; should not become universal game-form law.

sources.title: ISO/IEC/IEEE 12207:2026 Software life cycle processes

sources.title: ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 Requirements engineering
sources.evidenceLimit: Current edition is expected to be replaced by a DIS/new edition; re-check before action.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 25010:2023 Product quality model

sources.title: SLSA Specification v1.2

sources.title: SPDX Specification 3.0

sources.title: Steam Playtest

sources.title: Steam User Reviews

sources.title: Android game optimization

sources.title: MDA: A Formal Approach to Game Design and Game Research

extractedIdeas: formal abstract tools as evolvable framework

sources.title: The Development and Validation of the Game User Experience Satisfaction Scale (GUESS)

sources.title: Games User Research Methods
